question.text: In the case of a minor signature mismatch on a service request, what does the RTA do?

answer.text: Asks for banker's attestation of signature
Gives 15 days for objection and then processes the request
Requires a fresh service request with notarized signature

explanation.text: The Logic: For a minor signature mismatch, the RTA provides a 15-day objection period to the holder and, if no objection is received within that period, proceeds to process the service request. The Trap: The treatment for a major signature mismatch is different and stricter. The workbook requires an original cancelled cheque with the name printed on it, or a self-attested copy of the bank passbook/bank statement, along with banker's attestation of the signature — not just an unsigned cheque. Note: The 15-day objection rule for minor signature mismatches and the document and banker-attestation requirements for major signature mismatches are set out on page 153 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
